title: Presentation: AI-Assisted Software Delivery: From Code to Production
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-assisted-software-delivery/en/mediumimage/infoq-live-medium-1795097572325.jpg"/><p>The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.</p> <i>By Garima Bajpaj, Martin Reynolds, Patrick Debois, Gunnar Grosch, Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/ai-staff-engineer/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795089716434.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Jordan Cutler, Senior Staff Engineer and Web Platform Tech Lead at Pinterest, presented how the role of a staff engineer changes when every engineer has access to the same AI tools.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/healthy-code-AI-tokens/en/headerimage/header-1794837764807.jpg"/><p>Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows.  Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: RIIIR: Rewrite It In *Idiomatic* Rust (with AI)
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/rust-ai-symposium-agent-client-protocol/en/mediumimage/NikoMatsakis-medium-1793279155828.jpeg"/><p>Nicholas Matsakis shares why AI makes Rust the ideal choice for modern production systems, skipping steep adoption hurdles via compiler guardrails. He discusses Symposium - an open-source, agent-oriented toolchain from the Rust Foundation - and demonstrates how the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardizes agent-to-tool extensibility across diverse enterprise developer workflows.</p> <i>By Niko Matsakis</i>

title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/NetWasm-0-10-Faster/en/headerimage/header-1794869319776.jpg"/><p>Summary: NetWasm, an ahead-of-time compiler from C# to WebAssembly, has reworked exception handling, bounds-check elimination, SIMD and division in its 0.10 series. Across more than 2000 benchmark cases, the project reports running in 0.41 times the time of Mono AOT’s WASI build.</p> <i>By Edin Kapić</i>

title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/discord-rust-rewrite-gpui-zed/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795054565892.jpg"/><p>Discord’s CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy recently announced rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native. The project eliminates layers of abstraction to directly leverage the device’s GPU, native mobile views, and a Rust core shared across platforms. Early results hint at a significant reduction in RAM usage and boot time for chat, voice, and streaming.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads, reducing daily shuffle fetch failures from approximately 750 to 20. The deployment also lowered compute costs by 10%, improved application runtimes by 14%, and reduced shuffle costs per task by nearly 90% through dedicated storage, replication, and data-plane optimizations.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/bookingcom-ml-data-platform-evolution/en/mediumimage/jabez-eliezer-manuel-medium-1792654383362.jpg"/><p>Jabez Eliezer Manuel discusses the 20-year evolution of Booking.com’s data management and ML platforms. He explains how they scaled MySQL topologies, sunset Hadoop for cloud architecture, and built high-throughput model serving and feature stores operating at 400B predictions per day. He also shares insights on personalization, interleaved experimentation, and their new agentic AI foundation.</p> <i>By Jabez Eliezer Manuel</i>

title: Vercel Releases UI SDK for Agents to Compose UI from Reusable Behaviors
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/vercel-ui-sdk/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794576155684.jpg"/><p>Vercel has released UI SDK in beta, an Apache 2.0 TypeScript library of more than 50 UI behaviors in @ui-sdk/core, with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, so agents can compose accessible components and operate them through a documented agent bridge.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-privatelink-tunnel-endpoints/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794476042263.jpg"/><p>AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-cassandra-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794921404342.jpg"/><p>Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: How Shopify Orchestrates AI-Powered Mobile App Development without Overloading Developers' Machines
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/shopify-remote-ai-dev/en/headerimage/shopify-ruvy-ruby-wasm-1794947458635.jpeg"/><p>To prevent AI development workflows from exhausting developer machines' resources, Shopify built Remote Dev, a remote mobile development environment that enables AI agents to independently build, test and maintain iOS and Android applications and in parallel.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/quik-2-streaming/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794907611481.jpg"/><p>Qwik 2.0 Release Candidate, published on 1 October 2026, replaces v1's HTML comment markers with two script blocks that hold state and virtual node data. It adds experimental out-of-order streaming, async useComputed$, and cacheable route loaders. Qwik's benchmarks show v2 at 1.23x vanilla JavaScript, versus 2.59x for v1. A migration command is provided.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/datadog-ai-agent-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408423767.jpg"/><p>Datadog is extending its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, allowing engineering teams to compare AI agent versions against real production traffic rather than relying exclusively on predefined evaluation datasets.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>
